summary.intent: Drive the FSM1/cipher-box umbrella issue #1963 (link-first sharing redesign) to completion using parallel Opus implementation subagents grouped into stacked PRs and Fable review agents, merging only when Greptile reports 5/5 and CodeRabbit has given a real review.
summary.outcome: All 22 sub-issues under #1963 were closed and the umbrella was closed out; roughly 20 PRs were merged across engine (core link fields, mint/read, api, claim/convert, append/permission, revoke/sweep, preview), web (share dialog, invite page), docs, and e2e slices, plus several follow-up fix PRs for defects the e2e suite and bot reviews surfaced (including engine bugs in cross-device write-plane recovery, stale render root names, and cut-bookmark handling).

repo: Two-device publish rule: the drain must re-resolve the scope root through the gate immediately before signing and sign above the highest observed sequence; a same-sequence-different-bytes record is a lost race, not a silent overwrite (crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs, net/publish.rs).

Grant-set commitment binds link entries (kind/deadline/conversionPermission/admissionCap) and ledger rows carry viaLink/granteeName/nameSource; a link entry always requires kind+deadline+admissionCap or the codec refuses it.

Conversion is ack-first: the owner engine only converts a mailbox claim after the mailbox DELETE answers removed:true, and the acked claim is persisted to a sealed owner-local ConversionRecord (kind 0x07) before any grant is minted.

Contact book keys a link's origin by the link's ephemeral identity key (LinkSource::Identity), not by its tag, because tags move under a write-scope cut/name wave; legacy LinkSource::Tag entries from older builds are a known residual window.

Cut sets (grantee_cut_set/link_cut_set) must match rows both by owner-attested identity and by contact-book-recorded encryption key/former subkeys, else a writer that strips its own row's signature or via_link can escape revocation.

The expired-link sweep must apply a grace period (link_sweep_grace) past the deadline before cutting a link, because a claim acked by one owner device may be invisible to another device's sweep until it converts.

Owner devices that did not run a write-scope cut keep a stale write-epoch floor and cannot open the new owner-write-blob; only a scope-pointer consult (on-access or tick-walk) raises the floor — this must be triggered whenever gated_write_plane can't open the blob, but a refused pointer consult must never be treated as 'no scope here' (a real blocker found in PR 2026 review).

A holder's render-tree node keeps the pre-conversion scope root name after a write-scope cut moves the root; the drain then waits forever on a name mismatch with no error — merge_grafted must update ipns_name from the healed bookmark.

A cut person's local bookmark makes the engine (and thus the invite/preview UI) treat them as already 'joined', hiding the join action even though ADR intent is that a re-join through a new link should work — engine must check the owner-signed set (personal blob presence), not just bookmark existence.

LEDGER_ROW_WIRE_BYTES must be sized for the full-width row (via_link + 255-byte grantee name + nameSource), not the bare 224-byte row, or the re-seal budget silently makes large scopes rotation-proof.

OPFS staging store needs per-file promise-chain serialization; concurrent createSyncAccessHandle calls on the same OPFS file throw, and clear() must snapshot per-file chains and skip live temp files to avoid erasing in-flight writes.

code.finding: gated_write_plane / write_plane_of_gated do not raise the write-epoch floor via pointer consult in all callers (three call sites: 1822, 3038/3049, 3464 promoted_root) — needs one shared helper to avoid duplicated inconsistent fixes.

refuse_an_unindexed_scope treated ResolveFailure::Rejected (from a refused/replayed scope pointer) as 'no scope here', letting a mint proceed over a live scope root — the mint probe must use a gate-only read that never runs a pointer consult.

revoked_rows/link_cut_set match a row by owner-attested identity OR (unattested/placeholder + contact book's recorded encryption key/former subkeys); this union is required so a write grantee that strips its own signature or via_link can still be reached by remove_grantees.

merge_grafted only renamed an existing render node, never updated its ipns_name when the bookmark's healed root name changed — caused #2023 (write-link holder stays read-only after conversion moves the root).

Sweep cap (MAX_SWEEP_CUTS=8) originally counted attempted cuts, not landed ones, via take(8); a failing publish leg could starve later scope roots forever and prevent cadence from advancing — fixed by counting only landed cuts.

workflow: Session-scoped CronCreate one-shot timers do not reliably fire across long idle periods; prefer detached background Bash scripts (run_in_background) with wait-until-timestamp loops for scheduled actions like CodeRabbit slot requests.

CodeRabbit allows only 1 included review per hour org-wide; an early request is silently lost (not queued), and a push to a READY PR auto-triggers a review that can steal the slot from an intended target — stagger pushes and always read the status comment's 'next review available in N minutes' before requesting.

An instant CodeRabbit 'Review finished' reply with no review object is not a clean verdict — must poll for an actual review object or walkthrough with 'no actionable comments' before treating a PR as CodeRabbit-clean.

Greptile re-scores the entire branch (not just the diff) after a rebase, surfacing concerns from merged main-line code; these must be triaged separately (verified via read-only review) rather than assumed to be about the PR's own diff.

Greptile's retrigger link does nothing via anonymous curl; it requires a signed-in GitHub browser session — drive it via the T3 Code preview browser tools (mcp__t3-code__preview_open/navigate) when available.

Nested sub-agents spawned by a lead reviewer/implementer report their results to the orchestrator (parent Claude), not back to the spawning agent — the orchestrator must manually forward each nested result via SendMessage so the lead agent can consolidate.

When a background Opus agent dies mid-task from an API rate limit or session interruption, resuming it via SendMessage often stalls with 'no progress' — spawning a fresh agent that cd's into the existing worktree to finish the work is more reliable.
Keep a MEMORY.md index under its size limit by periodically trimming long index lines; entries past ~200 lines get truncated and become invisible to future sessions.

friction: Session cron timers (CronCreate one-shot wakeups) silently failed to fire across idle periods multiple times, requiring the user to notice and prompt ('did you get stuck?') before switching to background Bash wait-scripts.

Repeated CodeRabbit slot collisions: auto-triggered reviews on pushes to already-ready PRs repeatedly stole the scheduled slot meant for a different PR, requiring constant re-polling and re-scheduling.
Greptile ran out of credits mid-session, blocking the user's stated 5/5 merge gate and requiring a policy exception (merge on CodeRabbit-clean + green CI alone) via AskUserQuestion.
Multiple rounds of Greptile findings on PR 1993 (share dialog) required five sequential fix-and-rescore cycles before reaching 5/5, each adding a push/poll round-trip.
Opus session rate limits (HTTP 429) killed several background agents mid-task simultaneously, losing in-progress work that had to be manually inspected and resumed from worktree state.
Disk space repeatedly dropped to critical levels (9.8-25 GiB free) from parallel worktree build caches (target/ dirs), requiring manual cleanup of merged/finished worktrees and root build cache.
The reviewer harness repeatedly refused to let Fable review agents write their findings.md scratch files, forcing reports to be delivered inline in the final agent message instead.

Fable review agents that fan out to nested sub-review agents (simplify/security/crypto/standards/spec) sometimes had those nested reports delivered to the orchestrator instead of themselves, requiring manual forwarding to avoid stalling consolidation.

A prior PR (1982) merged on a false-positive CodeRabbit verdict (instant 'Review finished' with no review object), caught by the user, requiring a retroactive CLI-based review pass on the merged commit.
open_items: Issue #1984 (reader cannot distinguish two records at its epoch floor) remains open by design, blocked by the broader resolve-outcome redesign it requires.
cipher-box-next PR #85 (ADR 0024 amendment for extra optional bookmark keys) was left for the user to accept/merge independently.
Staging E2E run (triggered at end of session) had not yet reported results for the new two-device link-first spec, which was previously only typechecked, not executed against staging.

PR 1987's Greptile-flagged residual: a write grantee can strip its own row's via_link reference before any wave, permanently escaping remove_grantees on that link (documented as an accepted/known window rather than fixed).

One low-confidence Greptile finding on PR 1999/PR 2026 area (a subkey shared between two contacts from a book written before the overlap-refusal fix) was left unaddressed pending a possible future ADR-level rule change.
ADR 0025 E1/E2 replay-after-revoke residual (claim replay via a live link before the next sweep) remains an accepted design gap per ADR, not fixed in this wave.
Web UI still lacks: since-column on grant list, per-link admission-cap edit surfaced fully, and a UI notice for the OPFS storage bug's residual edge cases beyond the #2000 fix.
